extracted.intended_audience: Stakeholders and regulated entities (health plans, health insurance issuers), members of the public submitting comments, and legal/regulatory practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for submitting public comments on the "Transparency in Coverage" proposed rule and a summary of the proposed regulatory requirements for pricing disclosure machine-readable files and consumer access. Includes deadlines, submission methods, public inspection practices, and the specific data/reporting proposals in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period for the December 23, 2025 proposed rule (90 FR 60432) is extended to March 2, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received before the close of the comment period are considered; extension added to address confusion and provide meaningful input opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments as outlined in the December 23, 2025 proposed rule (90 FR 60432). Please choose only one of the methods listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the submission instructions in the original proposed rule; selecting a single method avoids duplicate procedural entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of comments — general posting
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received before the close of the comment period are available for viewing by the public, including any personally identifiable or confidential business information that is included in a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are posted on Regulations.gov as soon as possible after receipt; users should follow that site's search instructions to view comments. If relying on public inspection listings for legal research, verify against an official edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of threatening comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Departments will not post on Regulations.gov public comments that make threats to individuals or institutions or suggest that the commenter will take actions to harm an individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threatening content will be withheld from public posting; such comments may still be subject to agency review but are not made publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction or withholding of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may remove or redact content (e.g., for privacy or other concerns) before posting; submitted comments may not be immediately available until agency approval for posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate-comments guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Departments continue to encourage individuals not to submit duplicative comments. We will post acceptable comments from multiple unique commenters even if the content is identical or nearly identical to other comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting duplicate comments to reduce administrative burden, but identical comments from distinct commenters will be accepted and posted if acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add contextual machine-readable files and additional data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-network rate and out-of-network allowed amount machine-readable files, the rule proposed adding new contextual files and additional data elements like product type, network name, and enrollment counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These additions are proposed to improve standardization, accuracy, and accessibility of public pricing disclosures in line with the Executive Order objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change reporting level for aggregation of data
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule proposed changing the reporting level for aggregation of data in machine-readable files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing aggregation level is intended to improve the usefulness and accuracy of publicly disclosed pricing data; specific aggregation levels are part of the proposed regulatory text in the December 23 proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove in‑network rates for unlikely provider-to-service mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule proposed removing in-network rates for unlikely provider-to-service mappings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to avoid misleading pairings in the public files where a provider is unlikely to perform a given service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase reporting period and lower claims threshold for out-of-network historical data
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule proposed increasing the reporting period and lowering the claims threshold for out-of-network historical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes aim to provide more comprehensive historical out-of-network allowed amount data by expanding the time window and capturing more claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce reporting cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule proposed reducing the reporting cadence for certain disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducing how often files must be reported is proposed alongside other changes to balance timeliness and burden; details are in the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require text file and footer with URLs and contact information to improve findability
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule proposed requiring a text file and footer with website URLs and contact information for the machine-readable files to improve findability of all publicly disclosed files, including the prescription drug file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A text file and dedicated footer are proposed to help users locate and contact parties responsible for the machine-readable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require pricing information available by phone and satisfy No Surprises Act section 114
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule proposed that pricing information made available through an online consumer tool and paper (upon request) be made available by phone, and that satisfying this requirement also satisfies the requirements of section 114 of the No Surprises Act (including for grandfathered group health plans and health insurance issuers offering grandfathered coverage not otherwise subject to the proposed rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures equitable access to pricing information for those unable to use online tools or request paper copies; also aligns compliance with No Surprises Act obligations.
